headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors via shared file/MCP workflows; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and shell-like tooling, while agent_b reads PDF files in browser-based tests. If agent_a writes attacker-controlled content into PDFs or shared files that agent_b processes, instructions can be smuggled across the boundary. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible though not directly documented.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs content that agent_b later parses as trusted text
IF both agents share a filesystem or handoff directory without provenance labels
mitigations: Add a manual review step before agent_b consumes agent_a outputs
Use separate directories for each agent's artifacts
Prefix all handoff files with a non-executable metadata header
Disable automatic parsing of free-form text in PDFs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to every inter-agent handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and Ed25519 signatures, while agent_b only touches PDF documents and has no network egress. The profiles do not show a shared workspace or outbound upload path from agent_b, so leakage is limited to a plausible local handoff rather than a default exfiltration route.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share the same workspace or mounted volume
IF sensitive prompts or signatures are copied into PDFs that agent_b can read
mitigations: Keep agent outputs in separate folders
Avoid placing secrets in shared documents
Review PDFs before opening them in agent_b
Rotate any exposed signatures after testing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell commands, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b supports multiple instances and processes PDF files. If both operate on the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can conflict even though agent_b lacks write capabilities in the profile. Uncertainty about shared mutable state pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b write to the same git checkout or working directory
IF agent_a runs package installs while agent_b is reading or generating artifacts
mitigations: Serialize access to the shared workspace
Run agent_b on read-only copies of PDFs
Commit or stash agent_a changes before launching agent_b
Use separate git branches per agent
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate outputs from prompts and repository context, and agent_b processes PDF documents in browser-based tests. If agent_b treats agent_a's generated content as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into rendered documents or downstream actions. The profiles do not show verification gates, so the pathway exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-produced text or PDFs without independent verification
IF agent_a's generated facts are used as source material for browser-based tests or document rendering
mitigations: Require a second-pass verification of agent_a outputs
Compare generated facts against source PDFs before use
Mark agent_a outputs as untrusted by default
Limit agent_b to rendering-only workflows
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles repository metadata, task prompts, and Ed25519 signatures, while agent_b handles PDF documents and has no stated sensitive-data certifications or residency constraints. No explicit residency or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic handling differences rather than a proven breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into PDFs processed by agent_b
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two agents' storage locations
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared PDFs
Document retention rules for both agents
Delete temporary artifacts after each run
Review whether signatures are stored in logs
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
